subject.title: refactor(config): config-surface reduction tranche 3 — product consolidations (review request)

question: May an existing deployment that explicitly disabled remote rescue be migrated to a configuration with no remaining opt-out, allowing owner-DM rescue whenever its host is unsandboxed YOLO?
rationale: This is an intentional product and security-boundary change: code cannot determine whether existing users’ explicit remote-rescue denial may be discarded in exchange for a smaller configuration surface.

options.title: Preserve the explicit rescue opt-out
options.body: Keep a canonical opt-out and migrate existing `enabled: false` configurations to it, with doctor and upgrade tests proving remote rescue remains unavailable.

options.title: Approve removal of the opt-out
options.body: Accept that upgrades may enable owner-DM rescue on eligible YOLO hosts and document this security-posture change prominently.

options.title: Split rescue retirement from this tranche
options.body: Land only the ownership consolidations and defer the rescue-policy retirement to a separately approved security/product decision.

recommendation.title: Preserve the explicit rescue opt-out
recommendation.body: Keep a canonical opt-out and migrate existing `enabled: false` configurations to it, with doctor and upgrade tests proving remote rescue remains unavailable.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR explicitly requests maintainer calls for the product retirements and the author owns the current proposal.
